mem.7:
- **May 7, 2023:** Caroline attended an LGBTQ support group. She found transgender people’s stories inspiring, felt accepted and supported, and gained courage to embrace herself.
- **May 8, 2023:** Caroline planned to continue her education and explore careers, especially counseling or mental health work. Melanie was busy with work and children and planned to swim with them.
- Melanie painted a lake sunrise in 2022. Painting helps her express feelings, be creative, and relax.
- **May 20, 2023:** Melanie ran a mental-health charity race; she found it rewarding and reflective.
- Melanie makes time for running, reading, or violin as daily self-care, which refreshes her and helps her be present for her family. She sees self-care as important but still a work in progress.
- In May 2023, Melanie’s children were excited for summer break; the family was considering a June camping trip.
- **May 25, 2023:** Caroline was researching adoption agencies. She has long dreamed of a family and providing a loving home to children in need. She intends to adopt as a single parent and was drawn to an agency supportive of LGBTQ+ adopters. She was excited and optimistic, aware it would be hard, and grateful for friends’ and mentors’ support.
- In the week before **June 9, 2023**, Caroline (surname unknown) spoke at a school about her transgender journey and encouraged students to engage with the LGBTQ community. She had been transitioning for three years. Students related to her story and were encouraged to be better allies. Caroline believes conversations about gender identity and inclusion matter; she wants to use her voice to foster understanding, acceptance, hope, and support, and to lift others up, as she was supported.
- **June 9, 2023:** Melanie praised Caroline’s advocacy and wanted to keep encouraging her. Melanie said her family motivates her and gives her love; Caroline cited friends, family, and mentors as her main supports. Caroline had known her friends for four years, since moving from her home country, Sweden. They supported her through everything, especially a difficult breakup. Friends’ names unknown.
- Caroline shared a photo described as a family posing in a yard; she said friends, family, and mentors support her, but it is unconfirmed who is pictured.
- Melanie said her husband and children motivate her. She shared a photo described as a man and little girl before a waterfall; identities are unconfirmed. She also shared a wedding photo of a bride holding flowers. She had been married five years as of June 9, approximately since 2018; wedding date unknown.
- Melanie shared a photo described as a man and woman eating on a blanket. She said the family played games, ate good food, and enjoyed time together. She cherishes family time and feels happy and alive; Caroline agreed time with loved ones brings happiness and gratitude and said family is everything to her.
- **June 23, 2023:** Caroline attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop on therapeutic methods and working effectively with trans people. She found it enlightening and valued professionals’ commitment to safe spaces.
- **June 27, 2023:** Caroline said a cross-and-heart necklace was a childhood gift from her grandmother in Sweden. It represents love, faith, strength, roots, and family support. A friend gave her a hand-painted bowl for her 18th birthday, around 2013; its colors and pattern remind her of art and self-expression.
- In the week before June 27, Melanie took her family camping in the mountains. They explored nature, hiked, roasted marshmallows, and enjoyed the view from the summit; her two younger children love nature. Her family also loves beach camping because it brings them closer.
- As of June 27, Caroline was exploring counseling/mental-health careers, especially work with trans people. Her journey and the support she received motivate her. Counseling and support groups helped her understand and accept herself and value mental health; she hopes to create a welcoming, safe place where people can grow.
- During **June 26–July 2, 2023**, Caroline attended an LGBTQ+ pride parade, felt belonging, and was inspired by the community’s happiness and growth. Conversations there encouraged her to use her story to help others; she was considering counseling/mental-health work.
- **July 2, 2023:** Melanie signed up for pottery, which she finds therapeutic and expressive. She later made a black-and-white flower-design bowl and felt proud. Pottery is important to her, not merely a hobby; clay work helps her express emotions and feels calming and joyful.
- As of **July 3, 2023**, Caroline was learning piano.
- **July 5, 2023:** Melanie took her children to a museum. They enjoyed the dinosaur exhibit, learning about animals, and seeing bones; the outing reminded her why she loves being a mother.
- Caroline is building a library for future children, with classic children’s books, stories from different cultures, and educational books. She looks forward to reading to them and opening their minds. Melanie’s favorite childhood book was *Charlotte’s Web*, for its message of friendship and compassion.
- Caroline says friends and family supported her transition with love, guidance, and acceptance, helping her accept and grow into herself.
- In the week before **July 6, 2023**, Caroline had a picnic with friends. On July 6 she said she was exploring counseling/mental-health work because she wants to help people and make a positive impact; she knows it can be difficult but rewarding.
- **July 10, 2023:** Caroline attended an LGBTQ conference. She met people with similar journeys, felt accepted in a welcoming community, and was grateful for it. It reinforced the importance of fighting for trans rights and raising awareness. She noted progress in LGBTQ rights but said more is needed and wants to make a difference.
- **July 12, 2023:** Caroline was still exploring counseling/mental-health jobs because she wants people to have someone to talk to. Her own mental-health struggles and the support she received inspired her to help others find support systems and navigate their journeys.
- On July 12, Melanie shared a photo of a book cover with a gold coin and said a book she read in 2022 reminded her to pursue her dreams. Caroline said books guide and motivate her and help her discover herself.
- Caroline’s favorite guidebook is *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt, a true story about a transgender girl and her family. It made Caroline feel connected and hopeful. She took lessons in self-acceptance, seeking support, and remembering that tough times do not last and hope and love exist.
- Caroline shared a photo described as a dog sitting in a boat on water while mentioning pets bring joy. Melanie shared a photo described as two little girls sitting on steps with a dog, then said her family has a dog and a cat; photos are not enough to establish identities. Their names are **Luna** and **Oliver** (which is which not specified). Melanie said they are sweet, playful, brighten the day, and liven up the house.
- Melanie shared photos of pink/purple running shoes. She said they are for running and that she has been running farther since their previous chat to destress and clear her mind. Running has improved her headspace and mental health, and she intends to continue. Caroline encouraged her to prioritize self-care.
mem.13:
Caroline and Melanie are close friends/supporters. Caroline says Melanie helps her notice happy moments; Melanie says Caroline makes struggles bearable. They attended a Pride festival together in 2022 and fondly remember it. On 17 Aug 2023 they agreed to plan a summer outing, perhaps catching up and exploring nature.

**Caroline:** Trans woman from Sweden; surname unknown. Had been transitioning for three years by 9 Jun 2023. Friends she knew since moving from Sweden, family and mentors supported her through transition and a difficult breakup; their love and acceptance helped her grow into herself. A cross-and-heart necklace her Swedish grandmother gave her as a child represents love, faith, strength, roots and family support. A friend gave her a hand-painted bowl for her 18th birthday, about 2013; its colors/pattern evoke art and self-expression. Blue is her favorite color and relaxes her.

Counseling and LGBTQ support groups helped her mental health and self-understanding. At a group on 7 May 2023 she felt accepted and inspired by trans stories. She attended an LGBTQ counseling workshop on 23 Jun, learning therapeutic methods and about working with trans people; she valued professionals’ commitment to safe spaces. She hopes to continue her education and explore counseling/mental-health work, especially supporting trans people and helping them accept themselves. She wants to create welcoming spaces and be someone others can talk to.

She attended Pride events/parades in late June/early July and on 11 Aug 2023; they brought belonging, happiness, pride and gratitude and strengthened her commitment to trans rights, equality, awareness and inclusion. At an LGBTQ conference on 10 Jul she met people with similar experiences and felt welcomed. The week before 9 Jun she gave a school talk about her journey, struggles and growth since coming out; students related, were encouraged to be better allies and responded positively. She wants her story to foster understanding and lift others up. She joined Connected LGBTQ Activists on 18 Jul; members plan campaigns/events and support one another. She finds it fulfilling and a platform for advocacy. She missed her city’s Pride parade on 15–16 Jul, but it reminded her people are not alone. On a hike, conservative religious comments upset her (17 Aug); supportive people helped her feel she would be okay.

Caroline’s longstanding dream is to become a single parent and give children a safe, loving home. She researches adoption and by 25 May 2023 was considering an LGBTQ-inclusive agency. A 14 Jul council meeting strengthened her resolve. She is hopeful and feels ready despite knowing it will be hard; friends and mentors support her. She collects children’s books for a future library: classics, books from different cultures and educational books. She loves books as guidance; favorite is *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt, an inspiring true story that gave her connection and hope, teaching self-acceptance, support and that hard times pass. A book-cover photo Melanie shared on 12 Jul reminded her to keep going. She says pets bring joy.

Caroline uses art to explore transition, her changing body and self-acceptance, including embracing imperfections; she values inclusive representation and telling her trans story through art. “Embracing Identity” shows a woman becoming comfortable and loving herself. She planned an LGBTQ art show for Aug 2023; a tree and bright sun painting inspired by an LGBTQ center represents unity and strength. On the weekend of 15–16 Jul she joined LGBTQ youth mentorship, mentoring a trans teen; she finds it rewarding and says it is going well. They attended a June Pride event; the teen’s face lit up at the love and acceptance. On 23 Aug 2023 Caroline said she applied to adoption agencies that week after attending an adoption advice/assistance group. She felt excited but nervous about parenting’s responsibility. Her guinea pig is Oscar; he likes vegetables, especially parsley. She loved horseback riding with her father as a child, riding through fields and feeling the wind; she has always loved horses. A self-portrait with a blue face, painted the week before 23 Aug, made her feel liberated and empowered; art helps her explore identity, be true to herself and is therapeutic. Supportive people, promoting LGBTQ rights and living authentically also give her freedom; she wants others to live authentically.

**Melanie:** Surname unknown. Married about 2018; had been married five years by 9 Jun 2023. Husband and children motivate her; she wants courage for her family. Cherishes time with loved ones. Wedding photo showed bride holding flowers; she recalls a loving, joyful ceremony with loved ones and treasured promising forever to her partner. Flowers evoke joy, growth, beauty, small moments and wedding decor. Photos showed a family picnic/outdoor meal and a man with a little girl at a waterfall; identities unconfirmed. Family games, good food and outings bring joy. Her family helped her through a move with practical help and love.

Has children, including a youngest daughter; her first steps reminded Melanie life is fleeting. Took children swimming (8 May 2023), to a museum (5 Jul; they loved dinosaurs, animals and bones) and pottery workshop (14 Jul; they made clay sculptures including a dog-face cup). They paint nature scenes together; on 8–9 Jul they painted a sunset with a palm tree and talked about nature. Children were excited for summer break; camping in June was considered. Family enjoys camping, mountain hikes, forests and beach camping. In the week before 27 Jun they camped in mountains, hiked, explored, roasted marshmallows and admired the summit view; younger children love nature. Camped 1–2 Jul; Melanie enjoyed unplugging. They look forward to campfires, stories and marshmallows. On a 2022 camping trip they watched the Perseid meteor shower, made wishes beneath a clear sky and felt one with the universe. They go to the beach once or twice yearly; a recent visit with children, and seeing them happy, was especially enjoyable. On 13 Aug 2023 she celebrated her daughter’s birthday with her children at a Matt Patterson concert; she loved his voice and songs.

Melanie values self-care, still a work in progress; it helps her care for family. Daily activities include running, reading and violin. After a mental-health charity race on 20 May 2023 she reflected on mental-health care. By 12 Jul she was running longer/farther to de-stress and clear her mind, improving her mental health. She painted a lake sunrise in 2022; painting helps express feelings, relax and create. Pottery is a major part of her life, not just a hobby: clay is calming, joyful, expressive and a sanctuary. Signed up for pottery on 2 Jul; made a black-and-white flower bowl and was proud. On 17 Aug she showed Caroline a colorful bowl designed to catch the eye and make people smile. Art brings comfort, happiness, fulfillment and learning. She has pets Luna and Oliver (which is the dog vs. cat unspecified); both playful and sweet. Favorite childhood book: *Charlotte’s Web*, for friendship and compassion.

On 23 Aug 2023 Melanie said her pets were well and she had recently added a cat named Bailey; she showed Caroline a photo described as Oliver, a black dog lying in grass with a frisbee. Oliver once hid his bone in her slipper. Melanie had fed a horse a carrot and painted a horse on a wooden wall; she loves painting animals, finding it peaceful and special, and admires horses’ grace. Both friends wished Caroline well on adoption; Melanie offered ongoing support.
mem.19:
Caroline: Transgender woman; surname unknown; Sweden is her home country. Had been transitioning for 3 years by 9 Jun 2023. Friends she has known since moving from Sweden, family and mentors support her; friends helped through a difficult breakup. Support and LGBTQ groups helped her accept herself. Values authenticity, community, equality and trans rights, and wants to pass support on. Melanie and Caroline are friends who encourage each other.

Adoption: Caroline’s longtime dream is to become a single parent and give children a safe, loving home. Researched inclusive LGBTQ-supportive agencies by 25 May 2023, attended an adoption council meeting 14 Jul, and applied to agencies during the week before 23 Aug with help from an advice group. On 13 Oct she told her mentor she felt ready to become a mother. On 20 Oct 2023, she passed adoption agency interviews and was excited that this brought her closer to having a family. On 22 Oct, she described adoption as giving children a roof, love and acceptance, and a safe home where they can grow. She sees it as giving back. She advised Melanie on 13 Oct to research agencies/lawyers, references, finances, medical checks and prepare for a difficult wait. Melanie had considered adoption after a friend’s successful adoption in 2022.

Career/community: Interested in counseling and mental health work to support people with similar experiences. Attended an LGBTQ counseling workshop 23 Jun and LGBTQ conference 10 Jul; both strengthened her interest. Attends pride events/parades (including 11 Aug); finds belonging, pride and acceptance. Spoke at a school event in early Jun about her trans journey; students were receptive and inspired toward allyship. Joined LGBTQ youth mentorship in mid-Jul and mentors a trans teen, helping build confidence; attended a June pride event with mentee. Volunteered at LGBTQ youth center by 28 Aug, shared her story and planned to continue; helped prepare children’s talent show. Joined Connected LGBTQ Activists 18 Jul, a group that meets, plans campaigns and supports members. Planned LGBTQ art shows for Aug/Sept 2023. Upset by religious conservatives’ comments during a hike around 17 Aug, but support helped.

Art/music/interests: Caroline has made art since about age 17; painting and drawing help express feelings and explore gender, transition and self-acceptance. Art conveys inclusion and her trans story. Works include “Embracing Identity” (woman’s journey to acceptance), tree/sun painting about LGBTQ unity, stained glass about growth, potential and togetherness, rainbow mural/eagle symbols of courage and freedom, blue-faced self-portrait (week of 14–20 Aug), August sunset painting, and red/blue painting where blended colors reject rigid gender binaries. Enjoys flowers/nature; blue is favorite color and calming. Tried abstract art by Oct. Plays acoustic guitar since around 2018; “Brave” by Sara Bareilles is meaningful. Learned piano by Jul 2023. Loves reading; favorite book “Becoming Nicole” by Amy Ellis Nutt helped her feel hopeful and learn self-acceptance. Building a library for future children (classic, multicultural and educational books). Childhood horseback riding with her father was special. Guinea pig Oscar likes parsley. Necklace from grandmother in Sweden, received when young, has a cross and heart and symbolizes love, faith, roots and support. Friend made her a painted bowl for her 18th birthday, about 2013.

Melanie: Surname unknown; married about 2018, married five years by Jun 2023; husband and children are her main motivation. Has a son and daughters. Family time, creativity, self-care and nature bring peace. Family enjoys camping, hiking, forests and beaches; camping includes campfires, stories and marshmallows. Camped 1–2 Jul 2023 and in the mountains before 27 Jun; saw Perseid meteor shower in 2022. Beach trips usually once or twice yearly. Family visited Grand Canyon on Oct 2023 road trip; son had an accident 14–15 Oct but was okay; family reassured frightened children. Trail outing with children 19 Oct helped Melanie relax. Youngest daughter’s first steps are a treasured memory. Volunteered with family at a homeless shelter 24 Aug.

Melanie self-care/creative interests: Runs, reads and plays violin daily when possible; running longer by Jul 2023 helped stress and mental health. Plays clarinet since childhood; likes Bach, Mozart and “Perfect” by Ed Sheeran. Painting and pottery are therapeutic; involved in art seven years by Sep 2023. Painted lake sunrise (2022), landscapes, flowers, horse, sunsets, sunflower; pottery includes flower plate (24 Aug) and colorful bowl shown 17 Aug. Injured in Sep 2023 and paused pottery; read Caroline’s recommended book and painted. Pink-sky sunset and blue abstract painting calmed her. Took pottery classes and brought children to workshop 14 Jul. Painted nature scenes with children, including palm-tree sunset 8–9 Jul. Favorite childhood book “Charlotte’s Web.” Pets include dog and cat Luna and Oliver (which name belongs to which unspecified); Bailey and Oliver also mentioned later. Oliver hid a bone in her slipper. Family has fed a horse. Enjoys live music; saw “Summer Sounds,” upbeat pop, and attended Matt Patterson concert with children for daughter’s birthday 13 Aug.

Shared/further details: Melanie and Caroline attended a Pride festival together in 2022. Caroline went biking with friends and saw a beach sunset 9–10 Sep 2023. Melanie’s photos included family outings/wedding, but pictured people are not always explicitly identified.

22 Oct 2023 conversation: Melanie congratulated Caroline on passing agency interviews and said wooden couple figurines she bought 21 Oct reminded her of family love. Caroline praised them and said families can be formed by blood or choice. She hopes to build a family by giving children a safe, loving home and providing love and acceptance, which everyone deserves. Caroline reflected that finding self-acceptance and transitioning were difficult; friends, family and mentors helped her through hard times and helped her discover herself. She wants to pass that support on; helping others feel comfort and grow brings joy. Melanie called her strong and inspiring; they affirmed mutual support and the freedom of being oneself. Caroline shared photos of a green-and-yellow-design clock and a painting with “happiness” written on it.
